look_here_first: Check the broad tree crown and a whole bipinnate leaf with generally few primary pinna pairs. Thorny twigs and pale cylindrical flower spikes lead to long straw-colored mesquite pods, not yellow spherical flower balls.

project_inclusion.range_basis: State-scale nativity supported by Kew POWO, but project exact 24-county three-county PASS proof was not completed.

best_field_traits: Woody native Texas mesquite with loose canopy and bipinnate leaves
Usually one or two pairs of main pinnae on each leaf; many relatively longer leaflets
Paired thorns may develop at nodes; not sufficient alone
Creamy yellowish flowers borne in elongated cylindrical spikes, NOT round pompons
Long straw-yellow to tan pods, frequently several together

comparisons.key_distinctions: Long pale flower SPIKES and long straw-colored pods, with relatively few leaf pinnae, distinguish mesquite from yellow-spherical-headed Vachellia. Hooked Senegalia prickles require different examination.

diagnostic_image_needs: whole bipinnate leaf showing 1–2 pinna pairs
paired spine attachment at node with ruler
ripe long pod and cross section
